description:
Look up what an occupation pays in Germany, combining JobJump's own salary aggregate with official German salary statistics. Use it when the user asks what a role pays or how pay differs by seniority; to judge a specific offer, use evaluate_salary_offer instead. Give the occupation in the user's own words in `job_title`; the server normalises German gendered forms and resolves the title to a JobJump job category.

Every returned figure is a separate labelled series with its own unit, statistic and vintage – read `series_id` and the matching provenance entry before describing a number. In particular: JobJump figures are annual gross euros and the official figures are monthly gross euros, so they must never be compared or combined without converting; and JobJump's own aggregate is built from per-seniority averages, so it contains no true minimum, no true maximum and no percentiles.

The official series is Germany-wide and full-time only. Neither dataset has a regional breakdown, so `search_region` changes no figure; the response says so explicitly. It covers the most-advertised occupations, so its absence for a given title is normal, not an error.

The tool returns gross figures only and gives no tax or take-home advice. For net pay, call calculate_net_salary. It does not return individual salaries, employer-level pay, or any personal data.

include_official_series.description: Include the official median and quartiles of monthly pay when a matching occupation exists. Set false to keep the response small when the user only asked about JobJump data.

job_title.description: Occupation or job title in the user's own words, German or English. Gendered German forms are normalised, e.g. 'Erzieherin' resolves like 'Erzieher'.

search_region.description: A German region the user themselves named. Accepted so the response can say so, but not applied: both JobJump's aggregate and the official statistics are nationwide figures. Never infer it, never pass coordinates.

seniority.description: Career stage to emphasise. 'entry' is JobJump's junior band, 'professional' its mid-level band, 'senior' its senior band, 'lead' its manager band. When omitted, all available bands are returned.

name: get_salary_benchmark

as_of.description: Vintage or reference period as published: 'YYYY', 'YYYY-MM' or an ISO date.

basis.description: Whether amounts are gross, net, or not a money amount.

dataset.description: Name of the dataset, e.g. 'Entgeltatlas' or 'JobJump salary aggregate'.

estimated.description: True when JobJump modelled or derived the value rather than observing or receiving it.

label.description: Short English name of what this series measures.

license.description: Licence or terms of use that apply to redistributing this series.

methodology_url.description: Public page describing how the series is produced, or null.

population.description: Who or what is counted, e.g. 'full-time employees subject to social insurance'.

sample_size.description: Number of underlying observations where JobJump knows it, otherwise null.

series_id.description: Stable key that series and values in this response refer to.

statistic.description: The statistic these values are. Read this before calling a value a median, a percentile or a maximum.

unit.description: Unit of every value carrying this series_id.

ags.description: Official German Kreis key (AGS) when one applies, otherwise null. Public administrative code, not a coordinate.

kind.description: Granularity the free-text input resolved to.

label.description: Coarse public name of the resolved region.

matched_input.description: The search_region text this resolution came from, echoed back so the user can see what was interpreted.

title: Get salary benchmark
